question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 66 and 11 respectively. If one of the numbers is 33, then find the other number.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

33 × Second Number = 66 × 11

Second Number = (66 × 11) ÷ 33

Second Number = 2 × 11 = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two numbers = 66

HCF of two numbers = 11

First Number = 33

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

**Calculation:**

Let the second number be x.

⇒ 33 × x = 66 × 11

⇒ x = (66 × 11) ÷ 33

⇒ x = 726 ÷ 33

⇒ x = 2 × 11

⇒ x = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of LCM and HCF

For any two numbers a and b, a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b). This rule applies only to exactly two numbers, not three or more.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators)
LCM = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime if their HCF is 1. Their LCM will always be equal to the product of the two numbers.
